summary: Benchmark fleet environment drift (NVIDIA driver/CUDA mismatch) causing noisy perf baseline results
description:
Issue summary
- Nightly baseline + ad-hoc reruns are showing high variance and occasional false-positive regressions (mostly p99 latency) that do not reproduce on a “known good” host.
- Root cause suspected/confirmed: benchmark runner is landing on GPU hosts with mismatched NVIDIA driver and CUDA runtime/toolkit relative to the pinned runtime build assumptions. This introduces performance differences and (worse) makes results non-comparable across runs.

Impact
- Perf baseline suite reliability is compromised (variance budget blown for multiple traffic shapes).
- perf-canary Slack summaries are generating noise and causing unnecessary escalation.
- Release qualification gates risk either missing real regressions (if thresholds are widened) or blocking on false positives.

Scope
- Benchmark fleet hosts used for:
  - Q1 2026 baseline runs
  - perf-canary nightly jobs
  - variance study reruns

Symptoms observed
- Same workload + same runtime SHA shows ~8–15% swing in TPOT p95 and unstable p99, correlated with region/host selection.
- “Severe regression” flagged in nightly run on 2026-02-11; later rerun on pinned host did not reproduce.

Preliminary findings
- At least two distinct environment profiles are present in the benchmark fleet:
  - Profile A (expected): NVIDIA driver 550.54.x + CUDA 12.4 userland
  - Profile B (drifted): NVIDIA driver 545.29.x + CUDA 12.2 userland
- perf-canary runner currently records runtime build metadata but does not hard-fail on environment mismatch; it also does not constrain scheduling to the expected profile.

Proposed enforcement (prevent drift from contaminating results)
1) Preflight hard-check in benchmark runner
   - On job start, capture:
     - nvidia-smi (driver version)
     - CUDA runtime version (libcudart)
     - OS image/AMI build ID
     - GPU SKU + MIG mode (if applicable)
   - Compare against suite “environment pin” (per baseline tag).
   - If mismatch: mark run as INVALID, upload metadata + logs, and fail job with explicit reason code: ENV_MISMATCH.

2) Fleet labeling + scheduler constraints
   - Label benchmark nodes with env_profile (e.g., env_profile=cuda124_driver550).
   - perf-canary + baseline runner must request a specific env_profile; disallow fallback.

3) Golden image / rollout discipline
   - Establish a single “Benchmark AMI” per quarter baseline tag.
   - Any driver/CUDA update must create a new env_profile and trigger baseline refresh policy per methodology doc.

4) Dashboards/alerts
   - Add a dashboard dimension for env_profile and surface mismatch counts.
   - Alert only on sustained mismatch rate (to avoid paging on single bad host) and route to Fleet owner + SRE on-call.

Remediation steps (clean up current drift)
- Identify and cordon/remove Profile B hosts from benchmark node pool.
- Force re-image or in-place upgrade to match Profile A.
- Re-run the last 3 nights for the top 5 baseline traffic shapes to confirm variance returns within budget.

Acceptance criteria
- 0% baseline/perf-canary runs executed on non-pinned env_profile.
- Runner artifacts include environment metadata and explicit validity flag.
- Variance for affected shapes returns to within the published variance budget for at least 3 consecutive nights.

References
- Slack: #incidents thread 1708533333 (false regression due to driver mismatch)
- Slack: #eng-runtime thread 1706123456 (p99 variance hypotheses; fleet mix/driver drift)
- Confluence: benchmark-methodology-and-variance-budget (variance budget + comparison rules)
- Confluence: ADR-001 baseline artifact versioning (environment pinning expectations)
